name: missing rows preserve the prior and report zero is valid
test:
import torch
prior = torch.tensor([0.25, 0.75])
confusion = torch.tensor([[[0.9, 0.1], [0.2, 0.8]]])
annotations = torch.tensor([[0], [-1]])
post = posterior_true_labels(prior, confusion, annotations)
assert torch.allclose(post[1], prior, atol=1e-6)
assert post[0, 0] > post[0, 1]
assert torch.allclose(post.sum(dim=1), torch.ones(2))

name: annotation NLL is finite and differentiable
test:
import torch
logits = torch.tensor([[2.0, -1.0], [-1.0, 2.0]], requires_grad=True)
confusion = torch.tensor([[[0.9, 0.1], [0.1, 0.9]]])
annotations = torch.tensor([[0], [1]])
loss = annotation_nll(logits, confusion, annotations)
assert torch.isfinite(loss)
loss.backward()
assert torch.isfinite(logits.grad).all()
try:
    annotation_nll(logits.detach(), confusion, torch.full((2, 1), -1))
except (ValueError, AssertionError):
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('all-missing annotations must raise')

name: chunked evaluation keeps the final partial chunk
test:
import torch
x = torch.arange(10).reshape(5, 2).float()
y = evaluate_in_chunks(lambda value: value + 1, x, 2)
assert torch.equal(y, x + 1)
try:
    evaluate_in_chunks(lambda value: value, x, 0)
except (ValueError, AssertionError):
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('nonpositive chunk size must raise')
assert not evaluate_in_chunks(lambda value: value.square(), x.requires_grad_(), 2).requires_grad

name: all-missing posterior keeps prior at nonunit temperature
test:
import torch
prior = torch.tensor([0.25, 0.75], dtype=torch.float64)
confusion = torch.tensor([[[0.9, 0.1], [0.2, 0.8]]], dtype=torch.float64)
annotations = torch.tensor([[-1], [0]])
post = posterior_true_labels(prior, confusion, annotations, temperature=2.0)
assert torch.equal(post[0], prior), 'temperature must not alter an all-missing prior'
unnormalized = torch.sqrt(torch.tensor([0.25 * 0.9, 0.75 * 0.2], dtype=torch.float64))
assert torch.allclose(post[1], unnormalized / unnormalized.sum())

name: annotation NLL averages observed reports rather than rows or joint likelihoods
test:
import torch
logits = torch.tensor([[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]], dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
confusion = torch.tensor([[[0.9, 0.1], [0.7, 0.3]], [[0.6, 0.4], [0.2, 0.8]]], dtype=torch.float64)
annotations = torch.tensor([[0, 1], [1, -1]])
loss = annotation_nll(logits, confusion, annotations)
expected = -torch.log(torch.tensor([0.8, 0.6, 0.2], dtype=torch.float64)).mean()
assert torch.allclose(loss, expected)
loss.backward()
assert logits.grad is not None and torch.isfinite(logits.grad).all()
